item.title: To win gold, Mikaela Shiffrin needed to hear these words
item.description: A gold medal dangled around her neck and an invisible burden had been lifted from her shoulders as Mikaela Shiffrin entered an NBC studio Friday afternoon.

item.title: Figure skating gold medalists welcome Alysa Liu to exclusive club
item.description: When Alysa Liu broke a 20-year medal drought for Team USA’s women’s figure skaters, a number of former champions were in the crowd, cheering her on. NBC News’ Stephanie Gosk spoke with 1992 Olympic champion Kristi Yamaguchi and 2002 Olympic champion Sarah Hughes about what this moment means.

item.title: Team USA men’s hockey team advances to gold medal game
item.description: The U.S. men’s hockey team dominated Slovakia, moving on to the gold medal match for the first time since 2010. They will take on Canada. NBC News’ Molly Hunter reports.

item.title: King Charles' statement on former Prince Andrew shows gravity of crisis for U.K. royals
item.description: King Charles III took the unusual step of personally signing his statement following the arrest of his brother, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor.

item.title: The Epstein saga engulfs Les Wexner — and the Ohio he helped build
item.description: Les Wexner's ties to Jeffrey Epstein have upended his legacy and put Ohio's political leaders under scrutiny.

item.title: Police Search Former Prince Andrew's Residence Amid Arrest
item.description: Former Prince Andrew was released from a police station after his stunning arrest on the morning of his 66th birthday after growing revelations about his alleged connections with late sex offender, Jeffrey Epstein. Andrew has not been charged, but police say he remains under investigation on suspicion of misconduct in public office. Officers also searched his house in Norfolk and his former royal residence near Windsor Castle. NBC’s Raf Sanchez reports for TODAY from Buckingham Palace.

item.title: U.S. stocks seesaw after Supreme Court strikes down most of Trump's tariffs
item.description: U.S. stocks experienced volatile trading Friday after the Supreme Court said that President Donald Trump could not impose sweeping tariffs under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act

item.title: Supreme Court strikes down most of Trump's tariffs
item.description: Delivering a major blow to President Donald Trump, the Supreme Court ruled he exceeded his authority when imposing sweeping tariffs using a law reserved for a national emergency.

item.title: 'The damage cannot be refunded': How small businesses are reacting
item.description: The Supreme Court’s decision to strike down many of President Trump’s tariffs came as a relief to business owners struggling under the weight of higher prices.

item.title: Trump vows 10% global tariff after Supreme Court ruling
item.description: The Supreme Court ruled Friday that President Trump exceeded his authority when he enacted sweeping tariffs on nearly every U.S. trading partner. NBC News’ Laura Jarrett and Christine Romans report.
